sights.n: Captain Tsubasa statues, Yotsugi–Tateishi (キャプテン翼 銅像)
sights.address: Yotsugi to Tateishi, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo (trail starts at Keisei Yotsugi Station)
sights.w: Nine bronze statues of Captain Tsubasa characters — Tsubasa, Hyūga, Misaki, Wakabayashi, Roberto — around author Yōichi Takahashi's home turf; the 'Twin Shot' statue lets you step in as Misaki. About 1.5 hours on foot from Yotsugi to Keisei-Tateishi.
sights.anime: Captain Tsubasa — author Yōichi Takahashi's hometown ward honours the football manga with a nine-statue walking trail

sights.n: Seiseki-Sakuragaoka — Whisper of the Heart pilgrimage (聖蹟桜ヶ丘 耳をすませば)
sights.address: Around Seiseki-Sakuragaoka Station (Keiō Line), Tama-shi, Tokyo
sights.w: The real town behind Studio Ghibli's Whisper of the Heart (1995): the station is the film's 'Suginomori', Iroha-zaka climbs to the 'Ghibli rotary', and a 'Seishun no Post' postbox stands by the station; walking maps are handed out locally.
sights.anime: Whisper of the Heart (Studio Ghibli, 1995) — the film's town is drawn from Seiseki-Sakuragaoka; station, slope and rotary are all recognisable

sights.n: Gashapon Department Store Ikebukuro Main Store (ガシャポンのデパート 池袋総本店)
sights.w: Bandai Namco's capsule-toy flagship — about 3,000 gashapon machines across 1,256 m², the most at any single location — dispensing Pokémon, Gundam, Ultraman and Doraemon figures, mostly ¥200–¥300.
sights.anime: Gashapon culture — Bandai's world-record capsule-toy store, stocked with anime and game character figures

sights.n: Tokyo Character Street, Tokyo Station (東京キャラクターストリート)
sights.address: First Avenue Tokyo Station B1 (Yaesu side), 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
sights.w: An underground row of 30-plus official character shops opened in 2008 on the Yaesu side of Tokyo Station — Pokémon, Studio Ghibli, Kirby, Chiikawa, Crayon Shin-chan, Rilakkuma and Hello Kitty, some with station-exclusive goods.
sights.anime: Character merchandise — one corridor of official stores for Pokémon, Ghibli, Kirby, Shin-chan, Chiikawa and more

sights.n: Oizumi Anime Gate, Ōizumi-gakuen (大泉アニメゲート)
sights.address: North-exit pedestrian deck, Ōizumi-gakuen Station (Seibu Ikebukuro Line), Nerima-ku, Tokyo
sights.w: Opened in 2015 outside Ōizumi-gakuen Station: life-size bronze statues of Astro Boy, Joe Yabuki (Ashita no Joe), Tetsurō and Maetel (Galaxy Express 999) and Lum (Urusei Yatsura) — Nerima's tribute to itself as the birthplace of Japanese TV animation.
sights.anime: Nerima 'Anime City' — home of Toei Animation and Mushi Production (Astro Boy, Japan's first TV anime series); statues of Astro Boy, Joe, Maetel and Lum
